discovery: Detection of baryon acoustic oscillations in the large-scale distribution of galaxies, establishing a standard ruler for cosmology

nominees.name: Daniel J. Eisenstein
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University (Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian), USA

motivation: In 2005 the SDSS luminous red galaxy sample (Eisenstein and collaborators) and the 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey (Cole, Colless and collaborators) independently detected the imprint of primordial sound waves in the clustering of galaxies. This baryon acoustic feature, a relic of the photon-baryon plasma frozen at recombination, provides a geometric standard ruler whose physical scale is calibrated by the cosmic microwave background and which is remarkably robust against astrophysical systematics such as dust and evolution. BAO confirmed cosmic acceleration by a method entirely independent of Type Ia supernovae and has become the backbone of precision cosmology, from BOSS and eBOSS to DESI, whose 2024-2025 results hint that dark energy may evolve with time. Eisenstein developed the theoretical framework and led the SDSS detection; Cole and Colless built and exploited the 2dFGRS. Their work transformed how we measure the expansion history of the universe.
